title: R' Yannai (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: We find in Shabbat 108b: R' Yannai sent to Mar Ukva, "Let the master send us some of those eye-salves (kilorin) of Mar Shmuel." Hyman concludes without doubt that this is not R' Yannai Rabba, and that it is impossible to say that he lived on even after Shmuel's passing and sent to Mar Ukva, who was Shmuel's student. Hyman considers it very likely that this R' Yannai is the one mentioned in Sotah 22a, who said regarding one who read and studied but did not attend upon scholars: R' Elazar says — R' Shmuel bar Nachmani says — R' Yannai says: such a person is a Samaritan. And in Keritot 5a: "R' Yannai said — for R' Yohanan said." Likewise Sukkah 50a: "R' Yannai said, R' Zeira said." And likewise Berakhot 55b, according to the reading of Dikdukei Soferim there, letter ז, that "R' Yannai said, R' Zeira said."

But what we find in Bava Kamma 36a — "Rav Ashi said, [supplied ה״ש] ... — Rav Yannai said: from the first clause too it is inferred" — Hyman calls a scribal error and says it should read "Ravina said," as explained in Dikdukei Soferim.

notes.text: The initials ה״ש in the Rav Ashi quotation are unclear. Hyman proposes Ravina rather than Rav Yannai in that passage.

All unsupported abbreviated personal titles, including the heading and every separate Yannai, Yannai Rabba, Elazar, Yohanan and Zeira occurrence, remain R'. The Sotah רשב״נ is retained as the inherited contextual Shmuel bar Nachmani expansion with R', without a fresh named Sotah title or identity verification. Every explicit Mar in the eye-salve exchange and both full Rav occurrences in the Bava Kamma quotation are retained; Ravina remains a proper name. II is the inherited label for ב), not a new chronological admission. Hyman's without-doubt exclusion, impossibility of the proposed survival, Shmuel-student relation, very-likely identification and Berakhot apparatus reading remain his arguments, with their force intact. The Sotah alternatives stay separated by dashes and the Samaritan classification is attributed, not adopted as an identity. The supplied Bava Kamma locator remains 36a beside the saved Davidson match on 37a. Three whole saved scalars were read: 36a, 198 characters, has Rava of Parzika addressing Rav Ashi with shema mina; the two 37a scalars, 217 and 155 characters, have Rav Ashi's ta shema and Rav Yannai's from-the-first-clause-too inference separately. The match does not prove that supplied ה״ש is a standard abbreviation for ta shema, and that supplied siglum remains unresolved rather than repaired. The earlier shema-mina guess and 36a bounded nonmatch remain historical, not global absence or retroactive PASS. The named 37a text reads Rav Yannai, not Ravina. Hyman definitely calls the reading a scribal error and says it should read Ravina, appealing to Dikdukei Soferim; that apparatus has not been newly collated and his correction is not adopted. Its Berakhot letter ז is retained as an apparatus letter. No legal continuation or proof text from the longer primary scalars is imported. All old English, mixed acronym/translation notes and the current unresolved-siglum note remain exact; this is one additive qualification. The p003 source hold remains.

The consulted printed notice, Hyman II, pp. 764–765, retains Bava Kamma 36a and the unclear ה״ש. The whole consulted Davidson match at 37a has Rav Ashi’s “Come and hear” and, separately, Rav Yannai’s inference from the first clause; this does not establish the supplied siglum’s expansion. Hyman definitely calls Yannai a scribal error and says to read Ravina, appealing to Dikdukei Soferim; the exact apparatus remains uncollated and his correction is not silently adopted. The whole Shabbat 108b eye-salve exchange confirms Yannai’s request to Mar Ukva, without proving Hyman’s chronology or importing Ukva’s omitted reply. Sotah 22a gives different classifications by Elazar, Shmuel bar Nahmani and Yannai; Hyman’s dash-separated abbreviation is not a serial transmission chain or a claim that all three use the last classification. Keritot 5a places Yannai’s saying before the explanation introduced by “for R’ Yohanan said”; Sukkah 50a directly gives Yannai in Zeira’s name. These local readings do not identify every namesake. Hyman’s “without doubt,” impossibility and “very likely” retain their force as his arguments; the Berakhot apparatus letter ז and the earlier unresolved-siglum notes remain unchanged.
